question.leadin: The Lateran Treaty governed the relationship between this country and its much larger neighbor.
question.text: Name this country, whose flag and coat of arms both depict a pair of crossed keys. Its head of state is elected through a conclave by the College of Cardinals.
question.answerHtml: Vatican City [or the Vatican City State, or Status Civitatis Vaticanae, or Stato della Città del Vaticano; prompt on the Holy See]
question.clue: Before this country was created, several men were called "prisoners" in the hill for which this country is named due to refusing to recognize authorities.

swap.text: This Ecumenical Council from 1545 to 1563 was the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation.
swap.clue: The Jesuits eventually gained control in the third and last period of this meeting which prepared a list of banned books and reaffirmed the seven sacraments.

question.leadin: This man, the successor of Gregory VII, carried on his predecessor's legacy of fighting against the sale of church offices after his 1088 election.
question.text: Name this pope best known for a rousing speech given at the Council of Clermont in 1095, in which he urged Christians to reclaim the Holy Land.
question.clue: This leader wrote a letter of instruction to the Flemish mentioning Adhemar of Le Puy, as reported on by Baldric of Dol and Robert the Monk.

swap.leadin: This council affirmed the legitimacy of the Eastern Catholic Church's rites and denied that Jews are solely responsible for Jesus' death.
swap.text: Name this Roman Catholic council that lasted from 1962 to 1965, which sought to relate Catholicism with changes in the modern world. It permitted vernacular languages' use in the Mass.
swap.clue: This event's second leader issued a reconciliatory joint declaration with Athenagoras I of Constantinople.

question.leadin: This treaty put an end to the "Roman Question."
question.text: Name this treaty between the Kingdom of Italy and the Holy See. This treaty recognized Vatican City as an independent state and allowed for financial compensation for the loss of the Papal States.
question.clue: This agreement comprised a three-article Financial Convention, a treaty of conciliation that made one side a neutral territory, and a concordat.

swap.leadin: God wills this bonus! answer some of the following about the event in which other people used that motto.
swap.text: The phrase Deus vult, or God Wills It, was used during by Pope Urban II during this council, which also led to the excommunication of Philip I of France. This council began a conflict led by Peter the Hermit against the Seljuk Turks.
swap.clue: Due to an adulterous relationship with Bertrade de Montfort, Countess of Anjou, Philip I was excommunicated at this church council, which was preceded by the council of Placentia.

question.text: This pope failed to secure church approval for Philip the Fair's campaign against the Knights Templar at the Council of Vienne, and also oversaw the papacy's move to Avignon.
question.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that outside of the church, there is no salvation.

swap.text: Calling upon Christians to retain orthodoxy and submission to the church, Robert the Monk records that a certain pope cried this phrase at the Council of Clermont, translating to "God wills it."
swap.answerHtml: Deus Vult [accept Deus lo Vult or Deus le Vult; some players may pronounce the “V” as a “W” due to classical Latin pronunciation]

question.text: The victorious confederation at Lepanto, led by Don Juan of Austria, was known by this name due to the participation of the Papal States.
question.clue: One of the members of a better-known group of this name won an important battle at Guinegate, also known as the Battle of the Spurs, and two year prior it defeated French forces at the battle of Novarra.

swap.leadin: The sale of these things inspired the rhyme, "When the coin in the coffer rings, the soul from Purgatory springs!"
swap.text: Name these remissions for sins, which Christians paid for in order to reduce time spent in Purgatory. The sale of these things was denounced in Martin Luther's 95 Theses.
swap.clue: They were first granted en-masse during the Council of Clermont for those soldiers who set out to the Levant.

question.text: This pope convened the 1095 Council of Clermont to advocate for the launching of the campaign.
question.clue: This pope allied himself with Roger I of Sicily, and he was heavily influenced by a delegation sent by Alexius I Komnenos.

swap.leadin: The only two teachings that were officially proclaimed to fall under this doctrine were the Immaculate Conception and Assumption of Mary.
swap.text: Name this doctrine under which, in certain matters, the pope is free from error.
swap.clue: What is the two-word name in English for the idea that the pope speaks for the whole church and cannot be in error?

question.leadin: This pope probably died of injuries associated with a painful fall from his mule at Narni.
question.text: This 14th century Pope once complained that he couldn't hear enough screaming when some rebellious cardinals were being tortured. He was opposed by Antipope Clement VII during the Western Schism.

swap.text: One of these splits in the Christian church arose when Gregory XI moved the papacy back to Rome. The split between the Orthodox and Catholic church in 1054 is known as the "Great" one of these.
swap.clue: This breaks and splits in the Christian church. The "Great" one resulted in the formation of the Catholic Church, while the "Western" one saw three popes ruling simultaneously.

question.leadin: Identify the following ecumenical councils from their theological statements.
question.text: This unrecognized council of 1409 failed to end the Western Schism, and its decision was superseded by the later Council of Constance.
question.clue: It was presided over by the Bishop of Palestrina, and came to a climax with a stirring denunciation delivered by Simon de Cramaud, the Patriarch of Alexandria, after which Baldassare Cossa successfully intrigued on behalf of Peter Philarghi.

swap.leadin: Identify these popes from descriptions FTPE.
swap.text: This man was elected pope during the 1417 Council of Constance. The successor to Gregory XII, he ruled until 1431 when he was succeeded by Eugene IV.
swap.clue: At the Council of Constance, this man was elected as sole holder of the papacy, thus ending the schism.

question.text: Saint Catherine of Siena persuaded this pope to move the papacy back to Rome. This pope also hired John Hawkwood to fight on his behalf in the War of the Eight Saints.
question.answerHtml: Pope <u>Gregory XI</u> [or Pierre-Roger de <u>Beaufort</u>; prompt on “<u>Gregory</u>”]

swap.leadin: After the election of Pope Clement V, Philip IV of France forced him to remain in that country, where his successor, Pope John XXIII built a Lavish palace in a city on the Rhone where he moved the Papal court,FTPE.
swap.text: Name this city in which 7 popes resided during its namesake papacy and in which a second line of illegitimate popes reigned during the Great Western Schism.
swap.clue: The man who ended this time period did so after reading a letter written by Catherine of Siena.

question.leadin: One factor in this event was one figure crowning Arnulf as Holy Roman Emperor.
question.text: Give the colloquial term for the 897 trial of Pope Formosus, in which the pontiff was charged with violating canon law by his successor and by a pissed-off Lambert II, who had previously been promised the crown.
question.clue: This event in which Pope Stephen VI put the rotting corpse of his predecessor, Formosus, on trial, declared Formosus's actions void, and ordered the body thrown in the Tiber.

swap.leadin: In order to secure temporal support after the end of Byzantine power in the west, this Pope applied to the new Frankish dynasty to uphold the claims of Rome.
